title: Uttarakhand
name: Uttarakhand
intro: Uttarakhand's assembly did not exist when the 1976 delimitation was made. The order gave the hill districts only twenty-two of undivided Uttar Pradesh's seats, and those twenty-two members formed the interim assembly when the state was created in November 2000. The seventy constituencies on the left were drawn for the new state by the Election Commission under the Uttar Pradesh Reorganisation Act, published in 2001, and contested twice, in 2002 and 2007, before the 2008 order replaced them.
The assembly map Uttarakhand used for its first two elections

map_caveats: This is one of a small number of states in the archive whose pre-2008 map is not the 1976 order. Uttarakhand's seventy constituencies were delimited by the Election Commission in 2001 for the newly created state, under section 10 of the Uttar Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2000, which amended the 1976 order through its Second Schedule.

The pre-2008 extents are given as the tehsils and kanungo circles each constituency was built from, summarised from the Commission's Final Statement II, which lists them down to individual land circles.
The two mapped layers are already in register with one another and have not been adjusted. Their outlines agree to an intersection-over-union of 0.97 as supplied.
Reservation status is taken from the Election Commission's records rather than from the constituency geometry, whose post-2008 reservation field reports one Scheduled Tribe seat where there are two.

Territory lineage is given on two footings, and each seat record states which applies to it. For 70 of the 70 pre-2008 seats the link is derived from the text of the two orders, which describe constituencies in the same vocabulary of tehsils, kanungo circles and patwar circles. For the remainder the successor shown is the one holding the largest share of the old seat's area, inferred from the boundaries alone.
Territory percentages are measured from the mapped boundaries in every case, and are areal shares, not shares of the electorate.
footnotes: Uttarakhand was created on 9 November 2000 from the hill districts of Uttar Pradesh. Its interim assembly comprised the twenty-two members elected from those districts to the Uttar Pradesh assembly of 1996; the seventy-seat map was first contested in 2002.
Reservation status reflects the category in force at the time of the relevant order, not any later reclassification.
